Follow up with members and after-sales customers to drive repeat purchases.

paragraphs: Before opening, organize and replenish merchandise and check displays. In the morning, greet customers and recommend products based on their needs, arranging fittings or trials. Handle the midday rush, verify promotions, and process orders. In the afternoon, follow up with members and manage returns and exchanges to drive repeat purchases. Before leaving, count inventory and review the day's transactions.

In one sentence: they turn merchandise into satisfying purchases. Their work includes greeting customers, recommending products, arranging fittings or trials, processing orders, handling returns, engaging members, and driving repeat purchases. It requires both conversation and constant movement on the front line of store sales.

AI will not replace retail salespeople, but it will reduce standardized roles. Self-checkout, cashierless stores, and online price comparison speed up routine transactions, shifting salespeople from processing payments and orders to experiential recommendations, trust-building, and member retention. People who only handle standard transactions face displacement, while those who can recommend and cultivate customers become more valuable.

paragraphs: A score of 5/10 indicates medium AI exposure in sales. Systems accelerate standard transactions, but people retain an essential role in experience and trust.

Medium-high exposure does not mean high risk. What gets replaced is the task of collecting payment and processing orders, not the role of managing customer experiences. People who recommend effectively and cultivate members become even scarcer as productivity rises. Salespeople who only stand at a counter and collect payment face the greatest risk.
Start in a store and practice product knowledge and sales conversations. Pure order processing is shrinking in the AI era, so develop customer-management skills early.
